messages.subject: png features inappropriately sized..
parts:
I see regular discussion of the problems with PNG scaling on them thar
interwebs. My own contribution to the stack of ugly graphs is here...

http://open-systems.ufl.edu/tsm/first-diff-occupancy/erp/ACURA.ERP.UFL.EDU.png

The responses I can find come down to "Don't do that", which is
dissapointing.


How do you-all generate web-destined graphics in ggplot2? Are there
tricks anyone might share?

If it's absolutely necessary, I can drop back to PDF, but that's (IMO) a
very poor general purpose web presentation format.

- Allen S. Rout

parts:
I almost exclusively export my graphs as png and haven't seen anything like that come out. I do remember having some issues when I adjusted the pixel dimensions and didn't adjust the pixel depth (resolution). 

#Save plot to file
png(filename="OUTPUTNAMEHERE.png", type="quartz", width = 2000, height = 1500, res=300)
print(NAMEofGGPLOT2-GRAPH-OBJECT-HERE)
dev.off()

Not had any issues since. As Mark said, some code/sample data is always welcome. 

Brandon

messages.author: 4e69b94a09c8cf3b
messages.subject: Re: png features inappropriately sized..
parts:
As far as I know, you have to scale the fonts yourself. Something along
the lines of
ggsave(filename="foo3.svg", plot=(dp + theme_bw(base_size=8)))

You likely want to pass an argument for size in geom_text aesthetic (so
now you are at the point where theme_bw and geom_text are split out from
the initial construction of dp). I don't know if there is a way to
change the base size default for geom_text in a theme definition.

You may want to consider handling the scaling of a cleanly produced plot
image using something such as ImageMagick convert. Wouldn't it be nice
if svg were a universal option?

On 07/27/2010 10:59 AM, Allen S. Rout wrote:

> Mark Connolly<mark_c...@acm.org> writes:
>
>
>> Maybe some example, fully functional code that shows the issue would
>> help us out some. I have generated many png files without issue.
>>

> I have seen the issue sufficiently well-trodden out on mailing lists and
> such that I figured it for an understood obstacle. My apologies, I'm an
> eager advocate of the repeatable example, myself. :)
>
> Below find a redacted chunk of data, a custom formatter for scales in
> bytes, a little folderol and the actual plot.
>
> The results I get for the three PNG ggsaves are visible in this
> directory:
>
> http://open-systems.ufl.edu/tsm/first-diff-occupancy/
>
> One is huge and well proportioned. The others are smaller and mutated.
>
>
> o3=structure(list(date = c("06/27/2010 ", "06/28/2010 ", "06/29/2010 ",
> "06/30/2010 ", "07/01/2010 ", "07/02/2010 ", "07/03/2010 ", "07/04/2010 ",
> "07/05/2010 ", "07/06/2010 ", "07/07/2010 ", "07/08/2010 ", "07/09/2010 ",
> "07/10/2010 ", "07/11/2010 ", "07/12/2010 ", "07/13/2010 ", "07/14/2010 ",
> "07/15/2010 ", "07/16/2010 ", "07/17/2010 ", "07/18/2010 ", "07/19/2010 ",
> "07/20/2010 ", "07/21/2010 ", "07/22/2010 ", "07/23/2010 ", "07/24/2010 ",
> "07/25/2010 ", "07/26/2010 "), amount = c(20734661L, 20735478L,
> 20737813L, 20741262L, 20743677L, 20746552L, 20748597L, 20807029L,
> 20864191L, 20866637L, 20869258L, 20870361L, 20874069L, 20875357L,
> 20933782L, 20934620L, 20992551L, 20994520L, 20998499L, 21001270L,
> 21004226L, 21113636L, 21116956L, 21119940L, 21123349L, 21125161L,
> 21127352L, 21129882L, 21235832L, 21242652L), node = c("EPPRD",
> "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD",
> "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD",
> "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD",
> "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD", "EPPRD",
> "EPPRD"), firstdiff = c(-817L, -2335L, -3449L, -2415L, -2875L,
> -2045L, -58432L, -57162L, -2446L, -2621L, -1103L, -3708L, -1288L,
> -58425L, -838L, -57931L, -1969L, -3979L, -2771L, -2956L, -109410L,
> -3320L, -2984L, -3409L, -1812L, -2191L, -2530L, -105950L, -6820L,
> 0L)), .Names = c("date", "amount", "node", "firstdiff"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(82L,
> 386L, 684L, 982L, 1278L, 1574L, 1873L, 2172L, 2471L, 2770L, 3069L,
> 3368L, 3667L, 3967L, 4267L, 4567L, 4867L, 5167L, 5467L, 5767L,
> 6069L, 6371L, 6673L, 6975L, 7277L, 7579L, 7881L, 8183L, 8485L,
> 8787L))
>
>
>
> bytes2<- function(x)
> {
>
> xs = x / abs(x)
> x<- abs(x)
> x<- x * ( 1024 * 1024)
> places = 2
> succession<- c("B","KB","MB","GB","TB","PB")
> y10<- floor(logb(x,1024));
> y10[y10==-Inf]=0
> labs<- succession[1+y10];
> db<- round(x /( 1024 ^ y10),digits=places);
> cute<- paste(db,labs,sep='');
> cute
> }
>
>
>
> library(ggplot2)
>
> omax = o3[o3$firstdiff==max(o3$firstdiff),];
> omin = o3[o3$firstdiff==min(o3$firstdiff),];
>
> m = mean(o3$firstdiff)
> std = sd(o3$firstdiff)
>
> ds = seq(m-3*std, m+3*std, by=std);
>
>
> dp = ggplot(o3) +
> geom_histogram(mapping=aes(x=firstdiff)) +
> opts(title = paste(
> "First difference of occupation for",omax$node,
> min(o3$date),"to",max(o3$date)
> ))+
> geom_vline(xintercept = ds ,color="red",alpha=.3) +
> geom_vline(xintercept = m ,color="green",alpha=.3) +
> scale_y_continuous("Count") +
> scale_x_continuous("First difference of occupation. Red lines are standard deviations.", formatter=bytes2 ) +
> geom_text(aes(omax$firstdiff, -1, label=omax$date,hjust=.7,vjust=.1))+
> geom_text(aes(omin$firstdiff, -1, label=omin$date,hjust=.3,vjust=.1))+
> theme_bw()
>
> ggsave(filename="foo.png")
>
> ggsave(filename="foo2.png",scale=.5)
>
> ggsave(filename="foo3.png",width=5,height=3)
>
>
>
>

> - Allen S. Rout
